mainTopic: Setting a שביתה under a tree without naming an exact spot: the size limits, the רב–שמואל dispute with a ברייתא on each side, and naming the trunk instead
overview: The amud opens by finishing the dispute about a תודה brought with eighty loaves: one view holds he meant one large offering, so nothing becomes holy. The גמרא then returns to רב's ruling that saying 'my שביתה is under this tree' is not enough. אביי limits that ruling to a tree with twelve אמות beneath it. רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע objects that the person might have picked an end section, so he sets the line at eight אמות; at seven or less, every possible four-אמה section shares the center cubit. Next the גמרא brings a ברייתא supporting רב: a traveler who did not mark out his four אמות may not move from his place. שמואל answers by setting that ברייתא in a case where the tree is 2004 אמות away, so the far side is outside his תחום. A second ברייתא supports שמואל: a man with עירובין to the north and to the south is limited by both. The גמרא answers that רב is not refuted, because רב תנא הוא ופליג. Finally the גמרא quotes the משנה's next case: one who sets his שביתה at the tree's trunk may walk 4000 אמות after dark.

steps.title: The other opinion: he meant one big offering
steps.stepSummary: This explains the reasoning of the second side in the dispute about a תודה with eighty חלות. That side holds the person intended one large offering, so none of the loaves become קדוש.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other Sage holds: he intends to bring one large offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes explaining a dispute it started earlier. It gives the reason of the opinion (understood as רבי יוחנן's) that none of the eighty loaves become sanctified.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion said the person really wanted forty loaves to be holy, so forty of the eighty take effect. This opinion disagrees. It says the person wanted all eighty as one big offering, and since that is not a valid offering, nothing takes effect. This sets up how we judge a person's vague or oversized intention.

keyTerms.meaning: The other Sage holds (introduces one side of a dispute)
A large offering (here, all eighty loaves together)
He intends

phrases.english: And the other Sage holds:
phrases.notes: Refers to רבי יוחנן's side of the dispute, which began on the previous amud.

phrases.english: he intends a large offering.
phrases.notes: He wanted all eighty loaves as one offering, so none of them become holy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-sided explanation of the תודה dispute, which began on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to this view, a person who brings eighty loaves intends one large offering, so no partial sanctification takes effect.

steps.title: אביי limits רב's ruling to a tree covering twelve cubits
steps.stepSummary: אביי says רב's ruling (that 'under the tree' is too vague for שביתה) applies only when the area under the tree is twelve אמות or more. If it is less, part of the residence is clearly known.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: They only taught this about a tree that has twelve cubits under it. But a tree that does not have twelve cubits under it is different, because part of his residence is clearly known.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי narrows רב's rule about a person who sets his שביתה 'under a tree' without picking an exact spot. He says the rule only applies to a big tree, one with twelve אמות underneath.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שביתה takes up four אמות. Under a twelve-אמה tree there are three separate sections of four: near, middle, and far. Since none of them overlap, we cannot know where he is. Under a smaller tree, אביי reasons that the middle four overlap both the near and the far four, so some part of his residence is certain.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this in the case of (a limiting formula)
Tree
Cubit (about 18-24 inches)
Part of his residence is recognizable/certain

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think אביי is saying the person picked a specific spot. He did not. אביי is saying that even without a choice, some cubit of his area is certain on a small enough tree.

phrases.english: Abaye said: They only taught this
phrases.notes: Refers to רב's ruling that 'under the tree' is not a valid שביתה.

phrases.english: about a tree that has twelve cubits beneath it,
phrases.notes: This is three full sections of four אמות that do not overlap.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בְּאִילָן שֶׁאֵין שְׁתֵּים עֶשְׂרֵה אַמָּה,
phrases.english: but about a tree that does not have twelve cubits,
part of his residence is recognizable.
phrases.notes: The middle four overlap the near four and the far four.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the תודה comparison back to defining the exact case of רב's tree ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב's invalidation applies only to a tree with twelve אמות beneath it. On a smaller tree the שביתה works, because part of the residence is certain.

steps.title: Who says he chose the middle four cubits?
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע objects that אביי assumed the person chose the middle four אמות. He may have chosen four at one end or the other, and those may not overlap.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע objected: How do we know he chose the middle four cubits? Maybe he chose the four on this side, or the four on the other side!
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע attacks אביי's reasoning. אביי's math only works if the person's four אמות are in the middle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On a tree of, for example, eleven אמות, the four at one end and the four at the other end do not touch each other. If the person may have picked either end section, no single cubit is guaranteed to belong to him. So אביי's number of twelve is too large.

keyTerms.meaning: He strongly objected to it
From where (do we know)?
The middle four (cubits)
This side
Perhaps

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua strongly objected to it:
from where do we know that he designates the middle four,
perhaps he designates the four on this side
phrases.notes: The four at the near end.

phrases.english: or the four on that side!
phrases.notes: The four at the far end. The two end sections may not overlap.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the hidden assumption in אביי's limitation.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that any tree under twelve אמות guarantees part of the residence.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: אביי's overlap only exists if the person chose the middle section. The two end sections can have no shared cubit, so nothing is certain.

steps.title: רב הונא's correction: the line is eight cubits, not twelve
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע restates the limit. רב's ruling applies from eight אמות and up. On a tree of seven אמות, every possible four-אמה section includes the center cubit, so part of the residence is certain.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע said: They only taught this about a tree with eight cubits beneath it. But a tree with seven cubits beneath it is different, because part of his residence is clearly known.
steps.whatsHappening: Since his challenge knocked down אביי's number, רב הונא offers a corrected number. A tree with seven אמות or less works for שביתה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With seven אמות, any four cubits in a row must include the fourth (center) cubit, so that cubit is surely his. With eight אמות, the first four and the last four do not overlap at all, so nothing is certain and רב's ruling applies. This answer fixes the flaw by requiring overlap no matter which section he picked, not only the middle one.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (rejects the earlier version and offers a new one)
Eight cubits
Seven cubits

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע's version replaces אביי's: saying 'my שביתה is under this tree' fails only when the area is eight אמות or more. At seven or less, every possible four-אמה section shares the center cubit, so the שביתה works.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rather, Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua said:
They only taught this about a tree
that has eight cubits beneath it,
phrases.notes: Two separate sections of four that do not overlap.

phrases.english: but about a tree that has seven cubits beneath it —
part of his residence is recognizable.
phrases.notes: The fourth cubit falls inside every possible section of four.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces אביי's twelve-אמה limit with a corrected eight-אמה limit, based on the objection.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Correction of the measurement (rewording of the limitation)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אביי thought any tree under twelve אמות works, assuming the middle section overlaps both ends.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a tree of seven אמות or less works, because then every possible four-אמה section shares the center cubit.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב's ruling applies to trees of eight אמות or more. At seven or less, the שביתה is valid.

steps.title: Each side has a supporting ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא announces that one ברייתא supports רב and another ברייתא supports שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא was taught that agrees with רב, and a ברייתא was taught that agrees with שמואל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move: it will quote two outside sources, one backing each side of the רב–שמואל dispute about 'my שביתה is under the tree.' This line is only an announcement; the actual sources come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After clarifying how far רב's rule reaches, the גמרא now looks for תנאים-level support. Both sides turn out to have a ברייתא, so this will not settle the dispute. It shows that each view has a basis in earlier teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא (a teaching from the time of the משנה that is not in the משנה itself)
In agreement with him; supporting his view
The two great early אמוראים who disagree here

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita in accordance with Rav,
phrases.notes: The first of the two announcements.

phrases.english: it was taught in a baraita in accordance with Shmuel.
phrases.notes: The ברייתא for שמואל is quoted later.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרַב, תַּנְיָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from defining how far רב's rule reaches to bringing outside support for both רב and שמואל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each side of the dispute has a supporting ברייתא.

steps.title: The ברייתא supporting רב: a tree accomplishes nothing, a named place works
steps.stepSummary: A traveler who says 'my שביתה is under that tree or fence' has said nothing. If he names a specific place, he walks there, gets the whole place, and gets two thousand אמות beyond it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone was traveling, and it got dark as שבת began. He recognized a tree or a fence ahead of him and said, 'My שביתה is under it.' He has said nothing. But if he said, 'My שביתה is in such-and-such place,' he may walk until he reaches that place. Once he reaches it, he may walk through all of it and two thousand אמות beyond it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא that matches רב. Saying 'under the tree' or 'under the fence' does nothing, exactly as רב ruled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The opening 'לא אמר כלום' repeats the משנה's own wording, which both רב and שמואל accept. So this line alone does not prove רב. The ברייתא then gives the contrast: if he names a 'מקום פלוני,' the whole named place becomes his home base, and he measures two thousand אמות out from its edges. The line that actually supports רב comes at the end of the ברייתא (step 9): if he did not mark out his four אמות, he may not move.

keyTerms.meaning: My שביתה, meaning my official 'home base' for שבת, from which the תחום is measured
He has said nothing; his declaration has no legal effect
Such-and-such place; a specific, defined spot
Two thousand אמות, the תחום שבת limit

steps.confusionAlert: 'He walks through all of it' means the entire named place counts as his home base, as if it were four אמות. His two thousand אמות start from the edge of the place, not from its center.

phrases.english: It was taught in accordance with Rav:
phrases.notes: The גמרא repeats the heading before quoting the ברייתא itself.

phrases.english: One who was coming on the road and it grew dark for him,
phrases.notes: שבת began while he was traveling.

phrases.english: and he recognized a tree or a fence,
phrases.notes: The tree or fence is within his two thousand אמות.

phrases.english: and he said: 'My residence is beneath it'
he has not said anything.
phrases.notes: This is the same wording as the משנה. The proof for רב comes at the end of the ברייתא.

phrases.english: But if he said:
'My residence is in such-and-such place'
he walks until he reaches that place.
Once he reached that place,
he walks through all of it
phrases.notes: The entire place counts as his base.

phrases.english: and two thousand cubits beyond it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Delivers the first ברייתא announced in step 5.
steps.raayaObject: רב's ruling that 'שביתתי תחתיו' has no effect
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a traveler naming his שביתה, which ends by saying that one who did not mark out his four אמות 'לא יזוז ממקומו'

steps.title: What counts as a clearly defined place
steps.stepSummary: A named place works only if it is clearly marked out: a mound ten טפחים high, or a hollow ten טפחים deep, between four אמות and a בית סאתים in size. In an undefined place he has only four אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: When does this apply? Only in a clearly defined place. For example, he set his שביתה on a mound ten טפחים high, between four אמות and a בית סאתים in size. The same is true of a hollow in the ground ten טפחים deep, between four אמות and a בית סאתים in size. But in a place that is not defined, he has only four אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes by limiting its own rule. A named place gives him the whole area only if the place has clear physical borders. Otherwise he gets just four אמות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A height or depth of ten טפחים creates a sharp boundary, so it is obvious exactly what area he picked. A tree's shade or a fence line has no such boundary, which explains the ruling in step 6 and fits רב. The size limits are four אמות at minimum (the basic size of a שביתה) and a בית סאתים at most (the largest area treated as one unit).

keyTerms.meaning: In what case were these words said? A phrase that introduces a limit on the rule
A defined place with clear borders
A mound
A valley or plain; here, a hollow sunk below the surrounding ground
An area of 5,000 square אמות, the size of the courtyard of the משכן
Four אמות, the basic personal space every person has

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא matches רב. Naming an undefined spot like 'under the tree' does nothing. A named place gives you the whole area only if it has clear borders (ten טפחים high or deep) and is between four אמות and a בית סאתים in size. Otherwise you have only four אמות.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the standard for what makes a chosen שביתה spot clear enough to work. That idea of a clearly 'known' area is the same concern behind the earlier discussion of how big the area under the tree is.

phrases.english: In what case are these matters stated?
phrases.notes: Introduces the limit on the rule.

phrases.english: In a defined place,
for example, where he set his residence on a mound
that is ten handbreadths high,
phrases.notes: Ten טפחים makes a clear boundary.

phrases.aramaic: וְהוּא מֵאַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת וְעַד בֵּית סָאתַיִם.
phrases.english: and it is from four cubits up to a beit sa'tayim.
And likewise a valley that is ten handbreadths deep,
phrases.notes: A hollow works the same way as a mound.

phrases.aramaic: וְהִיא מֵאַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת וְעַד בֵּית סָאתַיִם.
phrases.english: and it is from four cubits up to a beit sa'tayim.
But in a place that is not defined,
he has only four cubits.
phrases.notes: He does not get the whole area, only four אמות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא and limits the 'named place' rule to places with clear borders.
steps.raayaObject: רב's view that an undefined spot such as 'under the tree' does not work for שביתה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's statement that an undefined place gives only four אמות and that a named place works only when it is clearly bordered

steps.title: A traveler who does not know the area can rely on one who does
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: if one of two travelers does not recognize the place, he hands his שביתה over to the one who does, and that one names the place.
steps.simpleTranslation: If there were two people, one who recognizes the place and one who does not, the one who does not recognize it hands over his שביתה to the one who does. The one who recognizes it says: 'My שביתה is in such-and-such place.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps quoting the same ברייתא it brought as support for רב. This line adds a practical case: a person who doesn't know the area can let a friend choose the spot for him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Naming a specific place only works if you can actually identify it. So a traveler who cannot identify any marked place relies on his companion, and the companion names a place for both of them. This is still part of the ברייתא's setup before the line that actually proves רב.

keyTerms.meaning: One who recognizes or knows the place
Hands over his right to set his שבת residence
Such-and-such place (a specific, named spot)

phrases.english: If there were two people,
one who recognizes the place and one who does not —
the one who does not recognize it
hands over his residence to the one who recognizes it,
and the one who recognizes it says:
'My residence is in such-and-such place.'
phrases.notes: He names a specific, marked place, as the previous step required.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיוּ שְׁנַיִם, אֶחָד מַכִּיר וְאֶחָד שֶׁאֵינוֹ מַכִּיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with a further case about naming a place.

steps.title: Without marking out his four אמות, he may not move
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא limits the whole rule: it works only if he marked out the four אמות he chose. If he did not, he may not move from his place. This supports רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: When does all this apply? When he marked out the four אמות he set. But if he did not mark out the four אמות he set, he may not move from his place.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the line of the ברייתא that actually supports רב. If a person chose a residence without marking out exactly which four אמות, he gets nothing there and is stuck where he is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב held that unclear four אמות give no residence at all. שמואל held that he still gets the area all the options share. This ברייתא says 'he may not move,' which sounds exactly like רב.

keyTerms.meaning: When does this rule apply? (introduces a limit)
Marked out, specified exactly
He may not move from his place

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the exact sentence the next step uses to challenge שמואל.

phrases.english: When does this apply?
When he marked out the four cubits that he set.
But if he did not mark out
the four cubits that he set,
he may not move from his place.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים — כְּשֶׁסִּיֵּים אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת שֶׁקָּבַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא with the line that proves רב.
steps.raayaObject: רב: four אמות that were not marked out give no residence
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ending of the ברייתא: 'לֹא יָזוּז מִמְּקוֹמוֹ'

steps.title: Does this ברייתא disprove שמואל?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether this ברייתא is a full refutation of שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this is a refutation of שמואל?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the ברייתא against שמואל. If the ברייתא says he cannot move, how can שמואל say he still gets something?
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל said a person with unclear four אמות still gets the overlapping area. The ברייתא says 'he may not move' at all. On its plain reading the ברייתא contradicts שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say?
A refutation from a source; a full disproof

phrases.english: Shall we say it is
a refutation of שמואל?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ending of the ברייתא to challenge שמואל.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's view that unclear four אמות still give the overlapping area
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says he cannot move at all, which leaves no room for שמואל's partial residence.

steps.title: שמואל: the tree is 2004 אמות away
steps.stepSummary: שמואל sets the ברייתא in a special case: the tree's trunk is 2004 אמות from where he stands. The far side of the tree is outside his תחום. So he may go only if he picked the near four אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל can tell you: What case are we dealing with here? Where it is 2004 אמות from where he stands to the trunk of the tree. If you put his residence on the other side of the tree, it is outside his תחום. So if he marked out the four אמות, he can go. If not, he cannot go.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers by putting the ברייתא in an unusual case. There, 'he may not move' happens for a reason unrelated to his argument with רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, unclear four אמות still share some overlap, so שמואל gives him that. But here the tree is at the very edge of his 2000 אמות. Only the four אמות on the near side are within reach, and maybe he meant the far side, which is outside his תחום. So unless he clearly chose the near side, he cannot go there at all.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? (sets a source in a special case)
The trunk or base of the tree
אמות (cubits)
The שבת boundary of 2000 אמות

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא does not disprove שמואל. In it, the tree stands right at the edge of the person's תחום, so an unclear choice might fall outside his boundary. Only that is why he cannot move.
steps.confusionAlert: שמואל is not agreeing with רב here. He is saying the ברייתא's 'he may not move' comes from the far-away tree and the תחום problem, not from a rule that unclear four אמות give nothing.

phrases.english: שמואל can tell you:
What case are we dealing with here?

phrases.aramaic: כְּגוֹן דְּאִיכָּא מִמְּקוֹם רַגְלָיו וְעַד עִיקָּרוֹ
phrases.english: Where there is, from where his feet stand to its trunk,
two thousand and four cubits,
so that if you place it
on the other side of the tree,
it ends up outside his Shabbos boundary.
If he marked out four cubits,
he can go,
and if not, he cannot go.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ שְׁמוּאֵל: הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by placing the ברייתא in a special case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Setting the source in a special case (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא means unclear four אמות never give a residence, as רב says.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא deals with a tree 2004 אמות away. The unclear choice might fall outside the תחום, so he gets nothing unless he picked the near side. שמואל's general rule still stands.

steps.title: A ברייתא about two עירובין supports שמואל
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that someone with two עירובין in opposite directions is limited by both of them. This matches שמואל's approach.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא was taught that fits שמואל. If a person made a mistake and set up עירובין in two directions, because he thought you are allowed to do that, or if he told his servants 'Go out and set up an עירוב for me,' and one put it to the north and one put it to the south, then: he may walk north only as far as his southern עירוב allows, and south only as far as his northern עירוב allows.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to support שמואל. It describes a man who ends up with two עירובין, one north and one south.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא does not throw out either עירוב. It treats both places as possibly his home for שבת, so he must respect the limits of both. This matches שמואל's approach, where an unclear שביתה still counts and he must stay within every possible limit.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא was taught in line with his view
He made a mistake
In two directions
He imagines / he wrongly thinks
Food placed to set one's שבת home base, which moves his 2000-אמה limit

phrases.english: A baraita was taught in line with Shmuel:
If he erred and made an eiruv in two directions,

phrases.aramaic: כִּמְדוּמֶּה הוּא שֶׁמְּעָרְבִין לוֹ לִשְׁתֵּי רוּחוֹת,
phrases.english: because he imagined that one may make an eiruv in two directions,
or if he said to his servants,
"Go out and make an eiruv for me,"
and one made an eiruv for him to the north
and one made an eiruv for him to the south,
he may walk north only as far as his southern eiruv allows,
and south only as far as his northern eiruv allows.
phrases.notes: Each עירוב limits how far he may walk away from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending שמואל against the ברייתא in step 11, the גמרא now brings a separate ברייתא that actively supports him.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's view that an unclear or double שביתה still counts, with the person limited by every possible place
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about two עירובין placed north and south

steps.title: Squeezed in the middle, he may not move
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends: if the two עירובין leave him exactly in the middle of his limit, he may not move from his place.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if they placed him in the middle of the limit, he may not move from his place.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes with its sharpest case. If the northern and southern עירובין box him in from both sides, he cannot walk anywhere.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Picture each עירוב placed 2000 אמות away from him in opposite directions. The northern one does not let him go south of where he stands, and the southern one does not let him go north. So both places truly count against him, which is the heart of the support for שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: They placed him in the middle
The 2000-אמה limit for walking on שבת
He may not move

phrases.english: And if they placed him in the middle of the limit,
he may not move from his place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This finishes the same ברייתא with its most extreme result.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's approach that both possible places limit him
steps.raayaSupportSource: The end of the same ברייתא: 'לֹא יָזוּז מִמְּקוֹמוֹ'

steps.title: Is this a refutation of רב?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether this ברייתא proves רב wrong.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this is a refutation of רב?
steps.whatsHappening: Since the ברייתא supports שמואל, the גמרא asks whether it also knocks down רב, who holds the other side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב holds that an unclear שביתה does not work at all. The ברייתא treats a double, unclear שביתה as working. That seems to go straight against רב.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say
A full refutation of an אמורא from a תנאי source

phrases.english: Shall we say this is a refutation of Rav?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The support for שמואל now becomes a challenge against רב.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's view that an unclear שביתה does not work
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא, which carries the authority of תנאים, rules that a double, unclear שביתה works. An אמורא normally cannot argue against a ברייתא.

steps.title: רב is like a תנא and may disagree
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רב has the standing of a תנא, so he may argue against a ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב is a תנא, and he disagrees.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits that the ברייתא does disagree with רב. But רב is allowed to disagree, because he has the status of a תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא does not try to explain the ברייתא in a way that fits רב. It simply accepts the disagreement. רב's special standing lets him side with a different תנאי view, so his opinion is not rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: רב has the status of a תנא
And he disagrees

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a general rule that any אמורא may argue on a ברייתא. It is a special standing that the גמרא gives to רב.

phrases.english: Rav is a tanna, and he disagrees.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This answers the challenge of step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Authority-based: the source is admitted to disagree, but רב is allowed to dispute it
steps.terutzHavaAmina: An אמורא cannot argue against a ברייתא, so רב must be refuted.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב has a תנא's standing, so he may disagree, and the רב–שמואל dispute stands.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא of two עירובין supports שמואל. רב is not refuted, because רב תנא הוא ופליג.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic answer found across ש״ס that protects רב from refutations based on a ברייתא.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: 'My שביתה is at its trunk' gives 4000 אמות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: if he named the tree's trunk as his שביתה, he may walk 2000 אמות to the trunk and 2000 more from the trunk to his house, a total of 4000 אמות after dark.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he said 'My שביתה is at its trunk,' he may walk from where he stands to the trunk, 2000 אמות, and from the trunk to his house, 2000 אמות. So he ends up walking 4000 אמות after nightfall.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to quote the next line of the משנה. This sets up a new discussion about naming the tree's trunk.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the vague 'under the tree,' the trunk is one exact spot, so the שביתה works. The trunk becomes his home for שבת, giving him 2000 אמות in every direction from it. His house is 2000 אמות past the trunk, so from where he stood he can cover 4000 אמות in all.

keyTerms.meaning: Its trunk (the base of the tree)
The place where he is standing
From when it got dark (once שבת began)
4000 אמות

phrases.english: If he said, "My residence is at its trunk,"
he walks from the place of his feet
up to its trunk, two thousand cubits,
and from its trunk to his house, two thousand cubits.
It turns out that he walks, after nightfall,
four thousand cubits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The רב–שמואל discussion is finished. The גמרא now returns to the משנה text to begin a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Naming the tree's trunk, an exact spot, as one's שביתה works. From where he stands he may walk up to 4000 אמות after dark: 2000 to the trunk and 2000 from the trunk to his house.
